messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

We need to simulate a lost-sales inventory system with the given initial stock, target_time, knowledge_cutoff (the same as target_time=100, knowledge_cutoff=100; horizon_time =130). The raw reports are all reports up to the knowledge cutoff. The knowledge cutoff is a timestamp (probably in same units as received_time). The raw reports include many records; some may have received_time > knowledge_cutoff? But knowledge_cutoff=100, so we only consider those reports whose received_time <=100. Then among those, for each event_id, we choose the highest visible revision (i.e., max revision number among those visible). That yields a set of chosen events. Then we keep only those chosen events whose event_time <= target_time (100). Then we apply those events in (event_time, event_id) order to simulate historical state, starting with initial_stock=12. Then compute after processing all events up to target_time (including up to 100) we need: stock_at_target (stock after events up to target_time). Also compute total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions - i.e., sum of unmet demand (lost) from demand events up to target_time (i.e., that were processed), counting only the demand that could not be satisfied because stock was insufficient. Also need to define stock_at_horizon after scenario: after we apply the future_schedule events up to horizon_time (130), presumably starting from the reconstructed historical stock at target_time, then process future_schedule events in (event_time, event_id) order (with event_time from 101 onward). After processing all future events up to horizon_time (including any that go beyond horizon_time? No events beyond horizon_time maybe up to 118 only; horizon_time is 130, so all future schedule events are within range). Then we compute stock_at_horizon after scenario, and also total future_lost (lost demand from future schedule only). Also find first_future_stockout_time: earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand (i.e., a demand event where demand quantity > stock at that point, causing lost). If no future demand unmet, return -1. Additionally the first_future_stockout_time must be from the scenario only, not counting historical stockouts.
